pages.text: 1. Identify which API the actual route uses: FE, GT EU, Mekanism J, MI EU, GrandPower or an item-only adapter.$p2. Check both the local face and the source/receiver face. Input/output terminology is relative to the Foundations buffer.$p3. Verify the appropriate blockPorts or itemCharging scope, input/output gate, old compat master toggle and GT direction toggle.$p4. Read the effective ratio and losses. An offer smaller than the conversion quantum cannot be rounded up.$p5. For GT, check voltage, amperage, shared tick budget, battery tier and loss-adjusted packet cost.$p6. Make space in the receiving buffer and test with a source that actually has stored power.$p7. Use the Power button or /foundations power inspect while looking at a machine. Reports simulate readiness; they do not transfer energy or force-load chunks.$p$(o)A disabled native-first adapter does not silently fall back to FE. A third-party source can still choose its own FE path if Calculator advertises it. This is a route-selection distinction, not a reason to add free conversion multipliers.$()$pActual server settings: live server values are available in the native or master Foundations reader.$p$(l:foundations_calculator:power/rounding)Transfer quanta and conservative rounding$()
